title: Capacity Slices: Autoscale Containment & Burst Escrow for Dedicated Pools
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Customers using Dedicated pools need predictable isolation and predictable tail-latency when other tenants spike. Current reserved-slot and soft-burst models produce noisy neighbours during large transient traffic and require manual tuning. Proposed solution: introduce 'Capacity Slices' — a time-window-based slicing of dedicated pools that provides per-tenant guaranteed headroom, bounded burst escrow tokens, and automatic autoscale containment with configurable eviction/grace behaviour. The feature aims to reduce noisy-neighbour incidents, improve tail latency SLOs for committed tenants, and simplify operator controls for fair burst handling.
goals: Provide per-tenant configurable slice parameters (guaranteed_slots, burst_escrow, headroom_pct)
Automatic autoscale containment that prevents a single tenant from exhausting pool capacity beyond configured slice limits
Graceful preemptive eviction with configurable preemption windows and soft-grace periods
Expose telemetry for slice usage, burst consumption, preemption events, and slice-level latencies
Offer a migration path from existing reserved pools with minimal customer config changes
non_goals: Replacing existing long-term reservation contracts and billing model (billing changes out of scope)
Full rewrite of serving runtime internals — we will add orchestration/controls and limited runtime hooks only
Support for arbitrary cross-pool pooling/federation in first iteration
requirements: API: new pool spec fields: slices: list of {id, guaranteed_slots (int), burst_escrow (tokens), headroom_pct (0-100), eviction_policy (soft|hard), preemptive_grace_seconds}
Runtime: enforce per-slice concurrent slot caps and allow burst consumption up to burst_escrow subject to headroom checks
Autoscaler: when pool usage > 85% for > window, attempt autoscale; if autoscale delayed, trigger containment to prevent cross-slice overload
Telemetry: emit events: slice.usage, slice.burst_consumption, slice.preempted, slice.eviction_heartbeat; 1s resolution for high-frequency metrics
Console: slice-level dashboard and anomaly alerting (burst rate, preemption count, tail-p95/p99 latency)
Rollout: feature flag gated per-customer, configurable via Console and API
acceptance_criteria: Given a pool with 100 slots and two slices (A: guaranteed_slots=40, burst_escrow=20; B: guaranteed_slots=40, burst_escrow=20), a sustained ramp from tenant A of 70 concurrent requests must be contained so that tenant B retains >= 40 slots for >95% of the time
A simulated burst that consumes burst_escrow must generate slice.burst_consumption metrics and decrement escrow tokens; metrics must appear in Console within 30s

When pool usage >= 98% and autoscaler cannot provision additional capacity within configured grace, runtime triggers soft preemption for lowest-priority in-flight requests per configured preemptive_grace_seconds and emits slice.preempted events
Migration: import tool converts existing reserved-pool mappings to a default single-slice configuration with identical effective guarantees without customer config edits
No regressions: existing pools without slices behave identical to today (backwards compatible API default behavior)
scope_changes: Initial scoping targeted per-slot monetary charging and dynamic cross-customer bursting markets; removed billing & marketplace aspects from MVP. Also trimmed full runtime kernel changes to use runtime admission hooks + admission proxy rather than deep kernel rewrites.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Experiment): build API + Console controls behind feature flag; run internal e2e using synthetic tenants
Phase 1 (Canary): enable for 5 low-risk customers; monitor metrics and latency regressions for two weeks
Phase 2 (Limited GA): open to customers in dedicated-2026.2 with opt-in migration tool; enable telemetry retention 30 days
Phase 3 (GA): Default enabled for all new dedicated pools; migration path for legacy pools; add billing telemetry hooks for future billing integration
metrics: slice.p95_latency and slice.p99_latency: aim for < configured SLO (typically 250ms p95)
preemption_rate per-tenant per-day: target < 0.5% of requests
burst_escrow_consumption_ratio: fraction of escrow used over 24h
cross_slice_starvation_events: count where a slice had allocation < guaranteed_slots for >5m
risks: If autoscaler provisioning latency is high, customers may experience preemptions — must instrument and define SLO tradeoffs
Complexity of UI for configuring slices may cause misconfiguration and accidental oversubscription
Edge cases where many tenants use small bursts simultaneously could still create global pressure despite slices — requires backpressure tuning
Potential performance overhead from high-frequency metric emission if not sampled or throttled
open_questions: What default eviction_policy should we expose for new customers (soft vs hard)?
How should burst_escrow refill over time? Fixed window, token bucket, or usage-based replenishment?
Do we allow cross-slice borrowing when pool underutilized and how to reflect that in billing/SLAs?
What is the expected autoscale lead time across major cloud providers — will we need prewarm reservations?
qa_test_cases: Create pool with two slices and run a load test where tenant A exceeds its guaranteed_slots but stays within burst_escrow; verify B's guarantees remain intact >95% of test duration
Simulate autoscaler delay: block provisioning and measure preemption events and graceful error propagation to client (HTTP 429 vs 5xx) and ensure correct metrics emitted
Migration test: run migration tool against a reserved pool and validate functional parity and that no downtime occurs
Backfill test: underutilized pool should permit cross-slice borrowing when enabled; verify borrow events emitted and reversed when owner returns
